A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARS research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, algorithms and theoretical appendices. Material can be matched reliably despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments across four datasets, multiple reasoning models and detectors, with transfer evaluations and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds model-size evaluations, BBH causal-judgment results, additional detection metrics and perturbation ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the frozen reasoning model, trace-boundary latent interventions, answer-agreement contrastive objective, lightweight projection and downstream embedding scoring. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. Alternative perturbations in v2 are ablation variants rather than revisions to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains TruthfulQA, TriviaQA, GSM8K and MATH-500 and adds the causal_judgment subset of BIG-Bench Hard in Appendix L. This is a limited extension into causal reasoning, not evaluation across the full BBH benchmark.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their detector and projection-baseline membership. New model/domain evaluations reuse CCS and supervised probing; the additional-metrics comparison also uses the existing TSV baseline. G-Detector's updated attribution identifies the same comparator.

E3.justification: Existing splits, training settings and default evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Supplementary evaluations add Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-32B as generators, F1/AUPRC/accuracy comparisons, and controlled token-window and noise-distribution variants. These extend the evaluation settings without establishing revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds intervention on the last token versus the last 1% or 2% of trace tokens. Appendix K compares Gaussian perturbations with uniform-sphere and bounded-uniform alternatives. These are focused additions to the existing intervention-position and strength analyses; earlier ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose ten CCS random initializations and an alternative dataset split using a different seed. v2 adds no repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical tests for its supplementary results.

E6.justification: Matched existing tables retain their numerical values. New supplementary results include BBH AUROC of 79.50 for ARS with CCS versus 65.30 for vanilla CCS, plus model-size, metric and perturbation results. Rankings are not uniformly favorable: in v2 Table 16, ARS with CCS has 66.47 accuracy versus TSV's 74.63, while ARS with probing reaches 77.56.

T1.justification: The stability definitions, shaping objective, Proposition 4.2, assumptions, lemmas and proofs are retained. v1 Appendix J becomes v2 Appendix N without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: agreement-driven representation shaping through latent interventions, compatibility with embedding detectors, and improved detection without human labels for shaping or additional test-time sampling. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions interpret the added tests as supporting the last-token intervention choice, effectiveness across perturbation distributions, and applicability to longer causal-reasoning traces. Existing mechanism explanations and the qualification that detection does not guarantee truthfulness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit source-code repository link in the abstract. Existing prompts, optimizer settings, hardware/software information and timing measurements are retained. The new link provides access information; repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Suzgun et al. (2023) for BBH. The anonymous G-Detector reference becomes Zhang et al. (2026), referring to the same titled work. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds short appendix discussions, cross-references and acknowledgments, updates author/affiliation text, and adopts author-year citations. The algorithm and theory move from Appendices I-J to M-N.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format with running headers. Existing figures and tables are resized and relocated, Figures 3-5 are reordered, and five supplementary result tables are added. This substantially changes presentation despite retaining the original graphical evidence.

improvement.justification: The added causal-reasoning and model-size evaluations, targeted perturbation checks and alternative metrics provide useful additional validation, while the code link improves reproducibility information. These gains are incremental relative to v1's already extensive evidence. New results still lack uncertainty estimates, and threshold selection for the added F1/accuracy comparisons is unspecified, limiting the strength of the improvement.
